legend.title: December to February trend minus the world average (+0.04) · mm/day per decade

caption: NASA GPM IMERG (via POWER) IMERG_PRECTOT · 1999–2025 · Sen's slope of the December to February mean of each year in each 2° square, after subtracting the world average of the same year (its own trend: +0.04 mm/day per decade). Differences are in mm/day, not in percent of the local average. Strong colour: passes the map-wide test for false alarms (Mann-Kendall with memory correction, q = 0.05). This map enlarges areas near the poles.

processing: read the whole globe for the variable from the temporal (location-chunked) store, in latitude bands covering the full time axis
coarsened to 2 deg cells with edges at multiples of 2 from -90 / -180
mean of December to February in each year 1999–2025 (December counts towards the next year) in each 2° square
minus the world average of the same year (area-weighted mean of every square with a complete record)
per-square Sen's slope and Mann-Kendall (Yue-Wang), BH FDR across squares (trend_stats.py)
provenance.caveat: Data: NASA GPM IMERG, rainfall estimated from satellites, about 10 km squares; the satellites changed in 2014 (TRMM to GPM) (the map averages them into 2° squares). The trend is a straight line through 1998–2025; it shows what changed, not why. The record is 28 years long, shorter than the 30 years usually used to describe a climate.
